title: Open Source and Closed Source Decisions
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Name a utility for recovering files after hardware loss.
options: There is not enough information to determine the result.
Backup and restore utility.
Backup OR restore utility.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Backup and restore utility.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of enqueue(X), enqueue(Y), dequeue() on an initially empty FIFO queue?
questions.answer: X is removed; Y remains at the front.
options: X is removed; Y remains at the front.
X is not removed; Y remains at the front.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: X is removed; Y remains at the front.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of sequential search in the worst case?
options: There is not enough information to determine the result.
This result cannot be obtained using the stated method.
O(n).

questions.prompt: After pushing A then B onto a stack, which is popped first?
questions.answer: B, because a stack is LIFO.
options: B, because a stack is not LIFO.
B, because a stack is LIFO.
B, because a stack is FIFO.
questions.feedback: Model answer: B, because a stack is LIFO.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: open source — Code distributed under a licence allowing inspection and specified reuse.
closed source — Source and modification rights normally controlled by owner.
licence — Legal conditions attached to software use.
vendor lock-in — Difficult or expensive dependence on one supplier.

blocks.title: Source availability
blocks.text: Open-source licences allow access to source code with specified reuse rights.

blocks.title: Control vs support
blocks.text: Closed-source vendors control release; support and integration vary by product.

blocks.title: Make a justified choice
blocks.text: Evaluate total cost, auditability, maintenance, expertise and obligations.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model answer
blocks.text: Relevant open-source licence can permit modification and inspection, allowing accessibility changes. Risk: the council must ensure support, security patching and licence compliance; source availability alone guarantees neither quality nor safety. Check: link each claim to the scenario and use precise OCR terminology.

blocks.title: Shared worked answer
blocks.text: A proprietary supported package may offer a service contract and managed upgrades; assess data export, recurring licensing, vendor lock-in and contract quality. Source model alone does not decide security.
